name: Google (Gmail / Workspace)
summary: You can create the OAuth client in 15 minutes, but the Gmail read scopes are 'restricted'. Going public requires brand verification plus a third-party CASA security assessment, which takes weeks and usually costs money.

verdict.label: Gated
verdict.headline: Testing works today for 100 users. Production Gmail access means a CASA security assessment and weeks of review.

approvalWait.appliesWhen: when publishing to production with sensitive or restricted scopes (e.g. gmail.readonly, gmail.send)

timeline.summary: Hands-on today; the production wait is dominated by verification and the CASA assessment

agent: Classify each scope you need as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted, and suggest narrower ones
Draft the scope justification text and the demo-video script for the verification form
Check that the homepage, privacy policy and authorized domains match before you submit
Validate your client_id against Google's authorize endpoint (Google rejects unknown clients without login)
human: Sign in to Google Cloud Console and create a project
Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
Record and upload the demo video showing the consent screen and each scope's use
Engage a CASA assessor (often paid) and complete the assessment
Answer reviewer emails; reviewers often ask for changes

steps.title: Create a Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Console → New project → APIs & Services → Library → Gmail API → Enable.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform)
steps.detail: Set the app name, support email, logo, authorized domains, homepage and privacy policy URL. Choose External. The app starts in Testing: only listed test users (max 100) can grant consent, and refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

evidence.note: 7-day refresh token expiry in Testing is documented

steps.title: Create OAuth client ID (Web application)
steps.detail: Add authorized redirect URIs. Exact match required, and https is needed except for localhost.

steps.title: Validate the client and run a test consent
steps.detail: Agent requests the authorize URL with your client_id. An unknown client gives an 'invalid_client' error; a valid one shows Google sign-in. Then a test user completes the flow with access_type=offline&prompt=consent to get a refresh token.

steps.title: Minimize scopes
steps.detail: If you can use gmail.send alone, or a non-Gmail alternative, you may avoid CASA. Restricted scopes include gmail.readonly, gmail.modify and gmail.compose.

evidence.note: Scope tiers listed on Gmail scopes page

steps.title: Submit for brand + scope verification
steps.detail: Requires a verified domain, a privacy policy describing Google data use (Limited Use), a scope justification and a demo video.

steps.title: CASA security assessment and Google review
steps.detail: Restricted scopes need a Cloud Application Security Assessment by an authorized lab, and it's re-done annually. Review rounds with Google commonly add weeks.

evidence.note: Duration is from community reports; Google gives no SLA

requirements.note: Homepage and privacy policy must be on an authorized domain you own.

requirements.item: Privacy policy with Limited Use disclosure
requirements.note: Must state compliance with the Google API Services User Data Policy.
Needed for sensitive or restricted scopes.
Restricted scopes only. Usually paid via an assessor lab; renewed yearly.

scopes.name: openid email profile
scopes.purpose: Sign in; no verification beyond branding

scopes.name: gmail.send
scopes.purpose: Send mail only: verification, but no CASA

endpoints.refreshTokens: Yes, with access_type=offline (7-day expiry while in Testing)

evidence.note: Discovery doc fetched: PKCE plain+S256, no registration_endpoint

blockers.symptom: 'Access blocked: app has not completed the Google verification process'
blockers.cause: The user isn't on the test-user list while the app is in Testing.
blockers.fix: Add them under Audience → Test users, or publish and complete verification.

blockers.symptom: Refresh tokens stop working after a week
blockers.cause: Apps in Testing get 7-day refresh tokens.
blockers.fix: Publish the app to production. You can publish non-verified for basic scopes.

blockers.cause: The demo video didn't show each scope being used in-product.
blockers.fix: Re-record showing the consent screen with the client ID visible and each feature using the data.

gotchas.title: Restricted scope = CASA every year
gotchas.detail: This is the single biggest cost in Google integrations. Design your agent so it can work with gmail.send or the Workspace add-on model if you can.

gotchas.title: Workspace-internal apps skip verification
gotchas.detail: If your users are all in one Workspace org, an Internal app skips verification. That doesn't help multi-tenant SaaS.

gotchas.title: Over 100 unverified users is a hard cap
gotchas.detail: An unverified app with sensitive scopes stops at 100 lifetime users.

tested.result: 302 → signin/oauth/error authError=invalid_client ('The OAuth client was not found')

uncertainties: CASA cost varies by assessor and tier; we haven't priced it.
The verification turnaround (4–12 weeks) comes from community reports, not a Google SLA.
